topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the introductory framing for the lecture series, outlining course structure and intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological Basis of Neoplastic Transformation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the accumulation of genetic alterations causes cancer through the progressive failure of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Pathology of Tumor Invasion, Metastasis, and Malignant Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how benign neoplasms advance to invasive and metastatic malignancies across histological boundaries.

topics.label: Nomenclature and Classification of Neoplasms
topics.groupedBecause: It sets out the standard rules, suffixes, and clinical conventions used to classify and name benign and malignant tumors.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the physiological, structural, and metabolic processes through which primary and metastatic tumors cause systemic disease and death.

topics.label: Comparative Incidence of Tumors Across Species and Tissues
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the prevalence and tissue distribution of neoplasms across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and Clinical Methods of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the diagnostic rationale, techniques, and practical efficacy of screening programs for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Administrative Wrap-Up
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the concluding framing, directing students toward practical sessions and upcoming lectures.
